title: Apex Insights — VPC & on‑prem deployment playbook (wip)
body:
Status: working playbook (internal draft)

Executive summary:
This document captures the proposed VPC/on‑prem private deployment for Apex Insights (analytics startup). Goal: deliver a single‑tenant, high‑availability inference cluster that meets 200 qps peak for 512‑token responses with P99 latency target <= 350ms for cached requests and <= 850ms uncached. Deployment mode: customer VPC with direct peering + on‑prem GPU nodes (customer DC) managed via Redwood Private control plane.

Key nonfunctional constraints and assumptions:
- Apex provides two racks of 8 x A10G GPUs (16 total) accessible over 10Gb internal fabric.
- Availability: N+1 across 2 AZs within the customer data center network (logical AZs).
- Storage: 50 TB NFS for model artifacts and KV cache persist.
- Network: BGP peering + IPSec fallback to Redwood control plane; MTU 9000 supported.
- Security: Customer KMS/HSM integration required for encryption at rest for model keys.
- Compliance: SOC2 + customer-specific HIPAA questionnaire in progress.

Sizing recommendations (initial):
- GPU pool: 16 x A10G; runtime configured with 8 concurrent model workers per GPU. Expected sustained tokens/s per GPU: ~1100 tokens/s (perf profile from benchmark run 2025-09-08).
- Serving nodes: 3 control-plane VMs (t3.large-equivalent) in customer management subnet for orchestration and telemetry proxy.
- Redis cache: 3-node cluster (2 cores, 8GB RAM) with persistence for KV prefix cache; will hold ~120GB active cache.
- Storage: 50 TB NFS mounted on model servers for checkpoint/quant artifacts; recommend ZFS with replication.
- Networking: Peering bandwidth reserve 1 Gbps baseline; burst to 5 Gbps during cutover.

Traffic profile and capacity planning:
- Baseline: 40 qps steady; Peak: 200 qps for 512 tokens average.
- Batching policy: continuous batching configured with max_batch_size 64 and timeout_ms 10 for low latency.
- Cache hit target: 60% for typical front-end prompt patterns => reduces GPU load by ~45%.

Terraform module notes (practical items for ops/SE):
- Module set used: tf-modules/vpc-peering, tf-modules/private-cluster, tf-modules/gpu-pool, tf-modules/telemetry-proxy.
- Recommended module variables (to pin in customer repo):
  - vpc_cidr = "10.40.0.0/16"
  - peering_auto_accept = false (customer must accept)
  - gpu_node_count = "16" (resources.tf will create placeholders only; actual provisioning by on‑prem team)
  - gpu_instance_type = "a10g-48gb"
  - model_storage_mount = "/mnt/models"
  - redis_replica_count = "2"

- Providers: require aws and local provider for initial cloud control plane records; include a provider alias for onprem ssh-based resources. Example: providers.tf should set version locks for terraform-provider-nv and terraform-provider-redwood (internal).
- State: Recommend remote state stored in customer's S3-compatible objectstore (MinIO) with server-side encryption and state locking via DynamoDB-compatible API (if supported). If not, use local encrypted state and periodic backups to S3.
- Secrets: Do NOT store plaintext KMS keys in tfvars; use vault lookup or pass via CI secrets.
- Module outputs to check after apply: vpc_peering_id, control_plane_endpoint, gpu_pool_ids, telemetry_ingress_ip.

Upgrade plan (runtime and model rollouts):
- Phase 0 (preflight): run redwood-inference /tools/preflight.sh (network checks, port range, kernel versions). Capture a preflight report and attach to Jira.
- Phase 1 (bootstrap): Deploy control-plane VMs and telemetry proxy; validate peering; create S3 buckets and permission sets; smoke test artifact upload.
- Phase 2 (gpu pool bringup): Register GPUs in maintenance mode; deploy runtime containers without model weights; verify health probes and KV cache durability.
- Phase 3 (model sync & warmup): rsync quantized models to /mnt/models; verify checksums; run warmup script to populate KV prefixes for selected prompt templates.
- Phase 4 (canary traffic): Route 5% traffic to the new cluster via traffic policy; monitor latency, memory growth, and errors for 48 hours; if regression > 5% in quality or > 10% latency SLO breach, rollback.
- Phase 5 (full cutover): Gradual ramp to 100% over 6 hours with autoscaling bands enabled.

Rollback strategy:
- Model-level rollback: re-pin previous model version in control plane and invalidate new cache entries.
- Node-level rollback: drain and revert to prior runtime container tag; reapply tf-modules/gpu-pool with previous ami/container image.
- Network rollback: remove peering route advertisements if BGP issues; fall back to IPSec tunnel.

Cutover checklist (short):
- Confirm KMS integration and test encryption/decryption with sample artifact.
- Validate MTU and jumbo frames across top-of-rack switches.
- Ensure NTP sync across nodes (drift < 50ms).
- DB and redis snapshot taken within 2 hours prior to cutover.
- Telemetry/metrics pipeline validated (prom exporter + traces).
- Oncall rotation (Apex Eng + Redwood SE) scheduled for 72 hours post cutover.

Known risks and mitigation notes:
- Risk: CPU contention on control-plane VMs during heavy telemetry. Mitigation: increase to 4 cores or offload metrics to remote collector.
- Risk: Model weight rsync saturates peering. Mitigation: throttle rsync and use rsync --bwlimit during business hours; prefer out-of-band physical transfer if > 100TB.
- Risk: Kernel/driver mismatch for A10G. Mitigation: preflight GPU driver compatibility matrix and perform upgrade in maintenance window with rollback AMIs.

Open questions for Apex (to resolve in next call):
1) Do they accept S3-compatible remote state in their datacenter? If not, provide plan for encrypted onprem state.
2) Confirmation of exact NIC model and switch firmware to validate RDMA/GPUDirect capabilities.
3) Any prohibition on outgoing connections from model servers to Redwood control plane (affects telemetry and auto-updates).

Estimated timeline (high level):
- Week 0: Finalize SOW and security checklist.
- Week 1–2: Network & peering setup, tf bootstrap.
- Week 3: Control plane and telemetry deployment.
- Week 4: GPU registration and model sync.
- Week 5: Canary & verification.
- Week 6: Production cutover.

Appendix — quick Terraform action notes for SEs:
- To upgrade provider dependencies safely:
  terraform init -upgrade
  terraform plan -var-file=secrets.auto.tfvars
  terraform apply -target=module.control_plane -auto-approve
- To perform a controlled tf apply of gpu pool only:
  terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool
- If state drift detected on gpu_count, do NOT manually import GPU nodes; coordinate with onprem hardware team to reconcile physical vs tf inventory.

Attachments and next steps:
- Attach perf logs from benchmark run (2025-09-08) and preflight script output to Jira PI-2143.
- Schedule technical review with Apex infra lead and Redwood SRE next week.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add full terraform module examples (variables.tf and outputs.tf) to internal repo PR.
- Draft short customer-facing one-pager summarizing SLA and support model.

Document history:
- 2025-10-15: initial draft (Nina)
- 2025-11-06: telemetry/redis sizing revision after perf retest (Marco)
- 2025-12-02: clarified terraform provider notes (Evelyn)

End of playbook draft.
